title: Adoption & Activation Sprint: 12‑Week Playbook (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, configurable 12-week (roughly 30/60/90) adoption & activation playbook for mid-market customers who have completed initial provisioning but need guided adoption. Draft intended for CS reps and solutions engineering to run joint sprints that accelerate time-to-first-value on Redwood’s inference product (hosted, dedicated, private).

Quick orientation (notes to self):
- Target customers: technical product teams integrating Redwood API + at least one dedicated instance or private eval.
- Goal: move from POC to first stable production route AND create clear renewal signals before month 10.
- Keep runbooks short, make handoffs to SRE/SE early for private deployments.

Success definition (North Star):
- Customer has 1 production-grade route receiving steady traffic (>= X requests/min for 7 consecutive days) and an agreed cost/LAT envelope documented in the console.
- Proxy metrics: integration tests passing + 2 different prompt templates validated + health score >= 80.

Suggested success metrics (quantitative):
- Time to first production request (target: <= 21 days)
- Number of routes with monitoring enabled (target: >=1)
- Prompt evaluation pass rate on critical testset (target: >=90%)
- Cost per 1k tokens vs baseline (target: within +20%)
- Health score components: usage, errors, latency, quality regressions (0-100)

Leading indicators to watch weekly:
- SDK install + CI run (green)
- First inference call from dev environment
- Baseline eval run completed (unit prompts)
- Access to logs & console confirmed (token-level breakdown visible)

Roles & responsibilities (recommended):
- CS Lead (owner): overall adoption plan, weekly check-ins, escalation owner
- Solutions Engineer: integration runbook, prompt engineering help, eval harness setup
- Customer Dev Lead: implement SDK, deploy route(s), set up monitoring
- SRE/Infra (when private/dedicated): assist with VPC/KMS and infra hardening

Milestones & acceptance criteria by phase:
Phase 0 (Pre-sprint: prep, days -7 -> 0)
- Deliverable: onboarding checklist completed (accounts, API keys, console access)
- Acceptance: Devs have tokens, sample route deployed to staging
- TODOs: CS to confirm billing limits, SE to allocate test model (JIRA: CS-4912)

Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4, activation sprint)
Week 1 (kickoff + environment setup)
- Kickoff agenda: introductions, success metrics, timeline, immediate blockers
- Tasks: install SDK, confirm network egress rules, run hello-inference sample, open support channel
- Acceptance: first successful inference call from customer staging environment
- Quick wins: show streaming + function-calling demo to stake interest

Week 2 (integration + prompt templates)
- Tasks: integrate into CI, add basic prompt templates for critical flows, run smoke evals
- Acceptance: CI inference test passing + prompt templates versioned in repo
- Notes: encourage use of prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce cost

Week 3 (observability + metrics)
- Tasks: enable route-level tracing in Console, configure token-level cost views, set alert thresholds
- Acceptance: alerts firing in staging when thresholds crossed; telemetry visible to customer and CS
- Slack snippet to post: "@customer-dev FYI we've enabled per-token breakdown and set a latency alert at 300ms p95."

Week 4 (first production cut & retro)
- Tasks: promote route to canary production, run 24h smoke load test, collect quality signals
- Acceptance: canary stable for 24h, no SLO breaches, CS collects notes for 30-day review

Phase 2 (Weeks 5-8, stabilization & scale)
Week 5-6 (scale plans & cost optics)
- Tasks: evaluate batching/quantization suggestions from Redwood Optimize; set autoscale/burst rules if using Dedicated
- Acceptance: automated scaling policy validated in staging; cost forecast updated

Week 7 (quality monitoring)
- Tasks: add regression prompt set to eval harness, configure alerts for quality drift, run A/B on two prompt variants
- Acceptance: baseline quality score recorded; threshold for regression alert set

Week 8 (customer enablement & playbooks)
- Tasks: hand off internal runbooks to customer engineering, run enablement workshop on console + rollouts
- Acceptance: customer has copy of runbook and confirmed internal owner for 24/7 on-call

Phase 3 (Weeks 9-12, optimization & renewal prep)
Week 9-10 (optimizations)
- Tasks: apply quantization recommendations, turn on prefix/KV caching for hot prompts, review cost impact
- Acceptance: token-cost per inference reduced by target or validated acceptable tradeoff with quality

Week 11 (business review prep)
- Tasks: prepare 30/60/90 slide summary (metrics, risks, wins), draft renewal health snapshot, list open action items
- Acceptance: CS Lead schedule QBR with customer executive sponsor

Week 12 (QBR & renewal signal checkpoint)
- Tasks: conduct adoption QBR (see agenda below), agree next 90-day roadmap and renewal checkpoints
- Acceptance: signed-off engagement summary + renewal signal flags set (green/amber/red)

QBR agenda (30-45 min compact):
- 5m: High level metrics (usage, cost, quality)
- 10m: Customer wins & value realized (stories)
- 10m: Risks & mitigations (open tickets, infra needs)
- 5m: Next quarter priorities + critical asks from Redwood
- 5m: Renewal/contract health & timeline

Renewal signals (operationalized):
- Green: steady or growing usage, few/no regressions, executive alignment
- Amber: usage plateau, 1-2 quality or cost concerns, scheduled migration to dedicated/private is pending
- Red: declining usage, multiple unresolved infra blockers, budget pushback

Sample email template (to exec sponsor ahead of week 12 QBR):
Subject: Redwood adoption QBR — progress & next steps
Hi <Name>,
Quick note: over the last 12 weeks we moved your team from sandbox -> canary production with X routes receiving traffic and an initial cost/latency envelope. Would you be available for a 30-minute adoption QBR on <date options> to review wins and confirm renewal timeline?
Thanks,
Leah (CS Lead)

Risk register (working):
- Data access delays (mitigation: escalate to SRE, JIRA CS-4950)
- Model quality regression after quantization (mitigation: A/B + rollback policy)
- Network egress issues for private deployment (mitigation: preflight checklist + dedicated SE time)

Handy checklists (copyable):
- Pre-kickoff: API keys, KMS access (if private), sample route working, console access for customer
- Cut-to-canary: tracing/alerts enabled, canary % config, rollback procedure documented
- Post-QBR: deliver slide deck, action item list, schedule renewal checkpoint 60 days before EOL

Open questions / discussion points (notes to self):
- Should we require SE hours for all private deployments in week 1? pros/cons at scale.
- Add a standard eval template per industry (search/rewrite/chat) to speed baseline quality checks. (tracked: ENG-1310)

Appendix: useful commands & links
- Quick eval harness: repo link (internal) -> TODO add public example
- Slack channels: #cs-onboarding, #cs-ops, #se-requests
- Typical Jira tickets to pre-fill: CS-____ (billing limits), CS-____ (infra access), ENG-____ (model variance)

Status notes: draft v0.3 — intend to iterate after 3 pilots. Please add comments in the Confluence version or ping in #cs-onboarding.

Intent for uniqueness: this file emphasises a sprint-style adoption flow, lean QBR, and explicit operational acceptance criteria tied to Redwood features (console, token-level cost, Dedicated autoscale). It is intentionally informal with checklists + repo/JIRA hooks to match Drive working-doc style.
